While UVC light can inactivate viruses and is used in controlled settings (e.g., water treatment, laboratories, and hospital disinfection robots), its effectiveness varies by material and geometry, and it is not established as a safe or reliable method for sanitizing personal protective equipment for public use [1]. Moreover, experts and health agencies advise that only highly concentrated UV (not found in normal sunlight) can inactivate viruses, and such exposure can damage human skin, so UV should not be used on the body to prevent infection [0].  [1]
